answer.rationale: A release shipped 2 hours ago coinciding exactly with p99 latency climbing 5x over 90 minutes. memory_b1 shows rollback cleared a similar checkout error spike without customer impact on the prior stable build. memory_b6 validates that staged gating catches regressions fast. Given settlement peak is active (heavy writes), the release is the most likely vector—it could have introduced write-path inefficiency. Rollback is the fastest path to restore the stable baseline while we're write-constrained. This preserves the write safety requirement (rolling back does not lose writes, it restores prior stable behavior) and uses our single intervention window decisively on the highest-probability cause. Regional failover and capacity addition are slower and more disruptive during peak settlement. Circuit breaker and read-replica routing don't address write-path degradation.
